newsitem.title: MEXICO: Santander link would aid Banco Mexicano - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Santander link would aid Banco Mexicano - analysts.

text.p: A capital injection from Spanish bank Banco Santander SA to Banco Mexicano would help the Mexican bank's precarious financial and operating situation improve, analysts said on Wednesday.
"The benefits for Banco Mexicano would depend on Santander's stake, but would be positive for the bank in any case," said Carol Milnes, an analyst with the Abaco brokerage.
Banco Mexico directors told Reuters that talks with Banco Santander were still underway.
"Talks with Banco Santander continue; they're confidential," said a Banco Mexicano director, who wished to remain anonymous.

"The merger would be very important, because Mexicano is still very vulnerable, despite 7.358 billion pesos in government support in the form of selling past-due loan portfolios to Fobaproa (the government bank support program)," said Marcos Chavez, an economist at the Colegio de Mexico.
Official figures place Banco Mexicano's capitalization index at 9.12 percent, or just above the required minimum of eight percent.
Banco Mexicano, like other Mexican banks, would have to raise capital to meet the required minimum once U.S. GAAP accounting criteria are introduced in Mexico next year.
One analyst estimated that Santander would need to acquire a 75 percent stake for Mexicano to be well-placed in the Mexican banking situation.

"Assuming Santander should take a 75 percent stake in Mexicano; the situation could be settled better and the way paved to raising capital by a friendly agreement with shareholders," said Alberto Camacho, an analyst at ABN AMRO Securities in New York.
